currentContext.strengths: World's largest manufacturer of motorcycles and scooters by volume for 25 consecutive years - scale leadership|Multi-generational brand trust across a diverse customer base in 53 countries|Wide domestic distribution reach - presence across 35 states and 52 international markets|Proprietary Connected Vehicle Platform bridging manufacturing intelligence with real-world vehicle telemetry and OTA updates|R&D centres in India and Europe supporting connected technologies and low-emission powertrains|Strategic partnerships and equity stakes reinforcing premium and electric-mobility ambitions - Harley-Davidson product partnership, and associate stakes in Ather Energy and Euler Motors|Supply-chain resilience investment via the Global Parts Center 2.0 expansion aimed at reducing customer wait times for parts
currentContext.strategies: Redesigning the manufacturing footprint to favour a high-yield portfolio concentrated on Premium Motorcycles, Scooters and Electric Vehicles, while continuing to expand market share in commuter motorcycles|Building supply-chain resilience and customer centricity in the Parts, Accessories & Merchandise (PAM) business through the Global Parts Center (GPC) 2.0 expansion|Pursuing global growth through an insight-led, hyper-local execution strategy tailored to individual international markets, leaning on joint ventures as growth engines (e.g. Colombia, Bangladesh)|Scaling and elevating the Hero brand in global markets via product-specific localised launch campaigns and expanded international product portfolio (Xoom, Hunk range)|Accelerating digital transformation - revamped global digital presence, Lead Management System (LMS) and Dealer Manager System (DMS) deployment for an integrated customer/dealer ecosystem|Treating AI as a core component of the 'Future of Mobility' strategy, not just a manufacturing-efficiency tool, to sharpen competitive edge|The Company maintains a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (published on its website) governing dividend decisions, and follows a two-tranche cadence each year - an interim dividend paid during the year and a final dividend recommended by the Board for shareholder confirmation/declaration at the Annual General Meeting.
currentContext.expansion: The Company is transitioning its legacy manufacturing footprint to be more agile, redesigning capacity to favour a high-yield mix of Premium Motorcycles, Scooters and Electric Vehicles while continuing to grow commuter-motorcycle share. Its manufacturing base comprises six facilities in India (Gurugram, Dharuhera, Halol, Neemrana, Haridwar and Tirupati) plus dedicated overseas plants in Villa Rica, Colombia (its first overseas manufacturing facility) and Jessore, Bangladesh (a joint venture with the Niloy Group), together supporting an approximate annual production capacity of 8.63 million units. A Center for Innovation and Technology (CIT) R&D facility operates at Jaipur, Rajasthan. On the supply-chain side, the Board approved an additional investment for a new Global Parts Center (GPC) 2.0 in Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh - featuring Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems, a Centralised Order Management System and Automated Sorters, with a conveyor network spanning over 5 km - to supplement the existing GPC at Neemrana and support the Parts, Accessories & Merchandise (PAM) business. Internationally, the Company achieved a historic export milestone (4,02,786 units, up 40.13% YoY), formally entered Europe (UK, Italy, France and Spain) with a Euro 5+ compliant portfolio, re-launched operations in Sri Lanka, started dispatches to Ecuador, and incorporated a wholly-owned subsidiary in Brazil that is building infrastructure and supply-chain networks for a full-scale commercial launch targeted for FY 2026-27. On the energy side, the Company expanded and planned further captive/wheeled solar power capacity across several plants (Dharuhera, Gurugram, Haridwar, Neemrana, GPC and CIT) as part of its energy-conservation programme.

one-line thesis: Hero MotoCorp delivered record FY26 revenue and PAT driven by a structural shift to scooters and exports, but faces immediate FY27 margin compression from West Asia-induced commodity spikes (aluminum/fuel) that outpace current 2% price hikes. The strategic pivot involves aggressive capacity doubling in scooters/EV and a ₹1,500 crore capex plan to capture high-growth segments while navigating a transitory profitability dip.
financial scorecard: Revenue: ₹12,797 cr (Q4, +29% YoY), ₹46,830 cr (FY26, +15% YoY); EBITDA: ₹1,856 cr (Q4, +31% YoY), ₹6,871 cr (FY26, +17% YoY); Margin: 14.5% (Q4, +30bps YoY incl. EV drag), 14.7% (FY26); PAT: ₹1,401 cr (Q4, +30% YoY), ₹5,268 cr (FY26, +14% YoY); Order Book: N/A (Retail demand outpaced dispatch, channel inventory reduced to ~5 weeks); Net Debt: Net Cash position (implied by strong ₹9,395 cr operating cash flow, +80% YoY); One-offs: EV business investment drag of ₹220 cr in Q4; Commodity headwinds began March impacting Q4/Q1 transition.
guidance: Revenue Growth: High single-digit industry growth expected in FY27; Hero to outgrow industry; Margins: Medium-term guidance 14-16% maintained despite short-term transitory pressure from commodities; Order Inflow: Strong momentum continuing into FY27; Capex: ₹1,500 cr committed for FY27 (Scooter/EV capacity, Parts center).
order book & pipeline: Channel inventory healthy at ~5 weeks (down YoY); EV inventory specifically in single-digit days; Retail performance outpaced wholesale indicating demand pull-through.
segment / subsidiary detail: Scooters: +48% YoY volume; EV: Volumes up 2.5x YoY; Premium (Harley range): +26% YoY; Exports: +41% YoY (4.02 lakh units, ~₹3,500 cr revenue); Commuter: Market share >90% in entry segments; Parts & Accessories: ₹6,200 cr FY26 (+6% YoY).
growth verticals / optionality: Scooterization trend (gaining share in 100-125cc); EV penetration (currently ~7% of industry, targeting 90% PLI coverage); Export expansion (Latin America, Africa, Bangladesh/Sri Lanka penetration); Aftermarket parts (targeting unaddressed 50% gray market).
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 commodity cost pressure: ~₹2,000/unit increase; Price hike taken: ~2% (₹700-₹3,500/model) in April; Gap: High single-digit BOM cost increase vs 2% price hike creates short-term margin headwind; Mitigation: LEAP savings, volume leverage, discretionary spend cuts.
capex / expansion: ₹1,500 cr committed for FY27; Focus: Doubling scooter capacity (Xoom/Destini), doubling EV capacity (VIDA brand) by year-end, ₹700 cr for new South India global parts center.
capital allocation: Dividend: ₹75/share final (Total ₹185/share for FY26, 70%+ payout ratio); R&D spend: ~2.5% of revenue (increasing YoY); Brand building: Ad spend +22% YoY; M&A/Investments: Continued support for EV ecosystem (Ather, Euler).
risks & watch-items: Commodity volatility (Aluminum, Steel, Gas) due to West Asia geopolitical tensions; Fuel price hikes impacting rural/urban demand sentiment; Regulatory uncertainty (ABS mandate, EPR draft notification); EV profitability timeline extension due to heavy capex/R&D.
management quality / tone: Confident on long-term structural growth (scooters/EV/exports) but cautious on short-term margin volatility; Transparent about commodity headwinds exceeding price hikes; Aggressive on capacity expansion to meet demand.
non-obvious takeaways: Retail growth outpacing dispatch indicates a rare channel de-stocking phase creating a clean base for FY27; EV loss per unit is declining quarter-on-quarter despite absolute loss increase due to scale; 'Saiyaara' movie product placement drove 120% growth in specific premium variants, highlighting marketing efficacy over pure product specs.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Commodity inflation (Aluminum/Steel) outpacing 2% price hikes, squeezing near-term margins for all OEMs. | TVS Motor Company | loser | Med | Similar exposure to aluminum-intensive scooter mix and export markets without the same scale of hedging or parts revenue buffer as Hero. |
| Rapid capacity expansion by Hero in scooters and EVs intensifies competition in high-growth segments. | Bajaj Auto Ltd | loser | Low | While Bajaj is strong in exports, Hero's aggressive scooter focus attacks a segment where Bajaj has historically been weaker, potentially capping Bajaj's domestic mix upgrade. |
| Hero's targeted attack on the unorganized parts market (50% gray market) via new logistics centers. | Samvardhana Motherson International | beneficiary | Med | As a key supplier of components and systems, increased OEM parts capture and higher vehicle production volumes directly benefit top-tier suppliers like Motherson. |

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- GST 2.0 reform (effective September 22, 2025) reclassified sub-350cc two-wheelers from the 28% to 18% tax slab with no sunset clause, providing a permanent structural improvement in affordability that management expects to keep supporting demand
- Recovery in replacement demand for commuter motorcycles, driven by a widening pool of aging vehicles nearing end of operational life plus continued permeation of GST-cut benefits, expected to continue into FY 2026-27
- Premium motorcycle uptrading accelerated by GST rationalisation lowering barriers for first-time buyers, sustained by a strong industry new-launch pipeline
- Rural demand recovery supported by an above-normal South West monsoon (108% of long-period average) and strong nominal wage growth
- Union Budget FY 2026-27 capital expenditure set to rise ~11.5% with continued focus on rural roads and national highways, which management views as structurally positive for mobility demand given the correlation between infrastructure expansion and two-wheeler demand in core segments
- Fiscal stimulus via personal taxation (zero income tax raised to annual incomes up to Rs 1.2 million) augmenting household purchasing power
- Monetary easing - cumulative 125 bps RBI repo rate cut through December 2025 - lowering finance costs for two-wheeler buyers
- EV segment penetration accelerating, aided by extension of the PM E-DRIVE subsidy scheme to July 2026, supporting the Company's VIDA electric business
- RBI has revised FY 2026-27 GDP growth projection down 30 bps to 6.6%, citing West Asia conflict-driven supply disruptions, inflation risk from volatile crude prices and possible weak monsoon (El Nino) as headwinds, though services-sector momentum, GST-rationalisation effects, rising manufacturing capacity utilisation and healthy corporate/financial-institution balance sheets are expected to keep supporting domestic demand

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- World's largest manufacturer of motorcycles and scooters by volume for 25 consecutive years - scale leadership
- Multi-generational brand trust across a diverse customer base in 53 countries
- Wide domestic distribution reach - presence across 35 states and 52 international markets
- Proprietary Connected Vehicle Platform bridging manufacturing intelligence with real-world vehicle telemetry and OTA updates
- R&D centres in India and Europe supporting connected technologies and low-emission powertrains
- Strategic partnerships and equity stakes reinforcing premium and electric-mobility ambitions - Harley-Davidson product partnership, and associate stakes in Ather Energy and Euler Motors
- Supply-chain resilience investment via the Global Parts Center 2.0 expansion aimed at reducing customer wait times for parts

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Commodity volatility (Aluminum, Steel, Gas) due to West Asia geopolitical tensions; Fuel price hikes impacting rural/urban demand sentiment; Regulatory uncertainty (ABS mandate, EPR draft notification); EV profitability timeline extension due to heavy capex/R&D.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Retail growth outpacing dispatch indicates a rare channel de-stocking phase creating a clean base for FY27; EV loss per unit is declining quarter-on-quarter despite absolute loss increase due to scale; 'Saiyaara' movie product placement drove 120% growth in specific premium variants, highlighting marketing efficacy over pure product specs.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Redesigning the manufacturing footprint to favour a high-yield portfolio concentrated on Premium Motorcycles, Scooters and Electric Vehicles, while continuing to expand market share in commuter motorcycles
- Building supply-chain resilience and customer centricity in the Parts, Accessories & Merchandise (PAM) business through the Global Parts Center (GPC) 2.0 expansion
- Pursuing global growth through an insight-led, hyper-local execution strategy tailored to individual international markets, leaning on joint ventures as growth engines (e.g. Colombia, Bangladesh)
- Scaling and elevating the Hero …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Commodity inflation (Aluminum/Steel) outpacing 2% price hikes, squeezing near-term margins for all OEMs. | TVS Motor Company | loser | Med | Similar exposure to aluminum-intensive scooter mix and export markets without the same scale of hedging or parts revenue buffer as Hero. |
| Rapid capacity expansion by Hero in scooters and EVs intensifies competition in high-growth segments. | Bajaj Auto Ltd | loser | Low | While Bajaj is strong in exports, Hero's aggressive scooter focus attacks a segment where Bajaj has historically been weaker, potentially capping Bajaj's domestic mix upgrade. |
| Hero's targeted attack on the unorganized parts market (50% gray market) via new logistics centers. | Samvardhana Motherson International | beneficiary | Med | As a key supplier of components and systems, increased OEM parts capture and higher vehicle production volumes directly benefit top-tier suppliers like Motherson. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Parts business] Parts Revenue up 30% YoY (PAM revenue Rs 1,296 Cr in Q1 FY26 to Rs 1,689 Cr in Q1 FY27), with the Hero Genuine Parts distributor network expanded to taluka level for rural accessibility, plus breadth expansion into non-vehicle allied revenue streams and premium riding gear / lifestyle accessories.
- [International launches] Xoom 125 launched in Colombia and Xpulse 210 launched in Nepal; VIDA made its global debut with entry into Nepal, supported by a launch anthem featuring Anna Sharma and Sabin Beast.
- [Fuel regulation readiness] Flex-fuel Splendor+ and HF Deluxe positioned as "future readiness", compatible with ethanol blends from E20 to E85.
